question.worked_solution:
First, let's remove the negative sign from the variable. To do this, we multiply both sides of the equation by $-1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{x}{7} & =-3 \\ (-1)\cdot (-\frac{x}{7}) & =(-1)\cdot (-3) \\ \frac{x}{7} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

In the equation above, $x$ is being *divided* by $7.$ To isolate $x$, we can perform the opposite operation, which is *multiplying* by $7.$ So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $7$ and simplify.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{7} & =3 \\ 7\cdot \frac{x}{7} & =7\cdot 3 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & =21 \\ \frac{\cancel{7}x}{\cancel{7}} & =21 \\ x & =21\end{aligned}
$$
